{"title":"Survey of automated image quality verification tools (open-source + commercial)","content":"### Plan overview
We will survey the landscape of automated image quality checking across **open-source libraries/models** and **commercial APIs/SaaS**, then synthesize into a structured comparison that highlights **capabilities**, **integration points**, and **limitations**.

### Output structure (final deliverable)
- **Taxonomy** of image-quality checks (technical IQA metrics, no-reference IQA, blur/noise/exposure, document/photo usability, aesthetic/perceptual, task-specific QA).
- **Open-source**: key libraries + model repos, what they detect/score, language/runtime, licensing, performance notes.
- **Commercial**: APIs/SDKs/SaaS offerings, quality checks, deployment (cloud/on-prem), pricing/quotas (where available), compliance claims, integration patterns.
- **Comparison table**: feature matrix + recommended picks by use case (e.g., “document capture usability”, “general no-reference IQA”, “pipeline QA at scale”).

### Quality criteria captured per tool
- Capabilities: metrics supported; detectability (blur, glare, low-light, occlusion, compression artifacts, resolution, framing, face presence, doc readability, etc.)
- Integration points: Python/JS/Java/C++ bindings, CLI, Docker, REST API, on-prem options, batch processing
- Limitations: domain transfer issues, calibration needs, reference-image requirement, latency/throughput, licensing constraints
